text: Every value f(m) belongs to the image subcomodule of f, with m itself supplying the preimage. The image is coaction-stable because f intertwines right coactions, matching [Milne’s subcomodule notion](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). This works over commutative semirings without flatness and does not assert that f reaches every vector of its codomain. Checks pass: [mem_range](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L388), [range_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L376).
Checks the existential image-membership criterion.
Checks the underlying module is the ordinary linear image.

If A is contained in B, then their images under the same comodule morphism satisfy f(A)⊆f(B). The coaction-compatible image construction adds no elements beyond the linear image, so ordinary image monotonicity applies. This accords with [Milne’s subcomodule definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) and requires no injectivity, flatness or finite generation. Checks pass: [mem_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L316), [map_sup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L256).
Checks image membership is witnessed by a source vector.
Checks the related preservation of binary joins.

A vector lies in the image subcomodule of f exactly when it equals f(m) for some m. Thus the bundled range has the ordinary image carrier; stability under the right coaction is additional proof data. This matches [Milne’s subcomodule notion](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), without assuming uniqueness of the preimage or surjectivity onto the entire codomain. Checks pass: [mem_range_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L394), [range_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L376).
Checks each actual value lies in the image.
Checks the full underlying linear image.

Forgetting the image subcomodule returns the range of f’s underlying linear map. It is constructed by imaging the full source subcomodule, so no extra closure or quotient is introduced. Compatibility with coactions gives the stability required by [Milne’s definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); the statement works over commutative semirings without flatness. Checks pass: [mem_range](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L388), [map_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L303).
Checks the ordinary image-membership rule.
Checks the underlying module of a general subcomodule image.

Taking the image of a subcomodule under the identity comodule morphism returns that subcomodule. Its carrier is unchanged, and stability is a property rather than new selectable data. This is the identity case of the [subcomodule construction](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), over the stated commutative semiring with no finiteness or flatness requirement. Checks pass: [mem_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L316), [map_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L355).
Checks image membership for the identity map.
Checks the corresponding composition law.

Imaging a subcomodule first under f and then under g gives its image under g∘f. The statement reduces to ordinary images of submodules, with composite coaction compatibility supplied by the comodule morphisms. This follows the [right-comodule convention](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); composition acts first by f, then by g, and neither map must be injective. Checks pass: [map_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L303), [map_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L347).
Checks reduction to linear images.
Checks the identity boundary of the composition rule.

The underlying module of the image subcomodule A.map f is exactly the linear image f(A). For an image vector, coaction compatibility transports A’s tensor-image stability to f(A). This implements [Milne’s subcomodule notion](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) over a commutative semiring; no flatness or injectivity is required, and the map need not preserve dimensions. Checks pass: [mem_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L316), [map_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L310).
Checks the image carrier elementwise.
Checks finite generation passes to the image.

A vector n belongs to the image subcomodule of A under f exactly when n=f(m) for some m∈A. This unfolds the ordinary module image used in the construction. The [subcomodule stability condition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) comes from colinearity of f, without adding other image vectors or requiring a unique preimage. Checks pass: [mem_map_of_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L322), [map_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L303).
Checks images of members belong.
Checks equality with the underlying linear image.

Containment of subcomodules is exactly containment of their underlying submodules. The order compares the same ambient vectors; the coaction-stability proofs impose no extra ordering relation. This is the subobject interpretation of [Milne’s definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), valid over the native commutative semiring without constructing inherited coactions on the subtypes. Checks pass: [le_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L132), [ext](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L139).
Checks containment is elementwise.
Checks equal membership determines equal subcomodules.

For a nonempty directed set of subcomodules, a vector belongs to its supremum exactly when it belongs to one member. Directedness absorbs each finite sum into a common member, as in [Milne’s filtered-union argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97). Nonemptiness matters: the empty supremum contains zero, whereas the empty union contains nothing. Checks pass: [coe_sSup_of_directedOn](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L180), [mem_sSup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L123).
Checks equality of the entire carrier with the union.
Checks unrestricted supremum membership uses finite sums.

The underlying module of an indexed supremum of subcomodules is the supremum of their underlying modules: vectors are finite sums from the family. Linearity extends coaction stability from each summand. This generalizes the finite-sum step in [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97), and includes an empty family, whose supremum is zero. Checks pass: [mem_iSup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L141), [sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L90).
Checks the finite-sum membership description.
Checks the binary specialization.

The sum of two finitely generated subcomodules is finitely generated: combine their finite module-generating sets. Its coaction remains stable by linearity. This is the finite-sum step of [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97), extended from vector spaces to commutative semirings. Finite means module generation, not a finite carrier set or finite ambient module. Checks pass: [sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L90), [finset_sup_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L242).
Checks the join is the underlying module sum.
Checks the finite-family extension.

The supremum of a set S of subcomodules has the module supremum of all members of S as its carrier. Thus it permits finite sums, rather than taking an arbitrary set union. This is the linear closure underlying [Milne’s finite-sum argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97); S may be empty or infinite and need not be directed. Checks pass: [mem_sSup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L123), [mem_sSup_of_directedOn](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L190).
Checks the finite-sum characterization.
Checks when membership simplifies to one member.

The binary join of subcomodules is their module sum. Each summand’s coaction lies in the sum’s tensor image, so linearity proves stability of the join. This realizes the finite-sum construction used in [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97). Max here denotes a least upper bound, not a choice of the larger of two comparable objects. Checks pass: [sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L90), [mem_sup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L96).
Checks the underlying sum.
Checks a member is a sum of vectors from the two inputs.

This operation forms the supremum of any set of subcomodules by taking the module span of their union. Coaction stability follows from stability of each member and linearity, extending the sum construction of [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97). Empty input gives zero; no directedness, flatness or finite generation is required. Checks pass: [sSup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L116), [mem_sSup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L123).
Checks the exact underlying module supremum.
Checks its finite-sum membership condition.

In a nonempty directed family of subcomodules, membership in the supremum means membership in one member. Every finite sum can be absorbed into a common upper member, which is the mechanism behind [Milne’s filtered unions](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97). The nonempty hypothesis ensures zero belongs to the union; no finiteness of the members is assumed. Checks pass: [coe_iSup_of_directed](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L158), [mem_iSup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L141).
Checks equality with the union of carriers.
Checks the general finite-sum criterion from which directedness simplifies membership.

The carrier of a nonempty directed supremum is the literal union of the carriers. Directedness makes that union closed under addition, while each member already has scalar and coaction stability. This is the union mechanism used by [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97), not an assertion that every arbitrary union is a subcomodule. Checks pass: [mem_iSup_of_directed](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L171), [iSup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L132).
Checks the elementwise union criterion.
Checks the supremum is computed on underlying modules.

Forgetting the binary join of two subcomodules gives the sum of their underlying modules. This is a defining equality of the join construction, whose stability follows by linearity of the coaction. It matches the finite-sum step of [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97); ordinary set union would generally fail additive closure. Checks pass: [mem_sup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L96), [finset_sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L215).
Checks the explicit sum decomposition.
Checks the corresponding finite-join carrier formula.

Subcomodules form a semilattice under inclusion with binary joins given by module sums. The inclusions into the sum and its least-upper-bound property are exactly those of submodules. This organizes the finite sums used in [Milne 4.7](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97); the native range-based stability proof needs no flatness of C. Checks pass: [toSubmodule_le_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L135), [sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Lattice.lean#L90).
Checks the inherited inclusion order.
Checks its join is the module sum.

The inverse transport correspondence takes a target subcomodule to its image under e⁻¹ on underlying modules, equivalently its preimage under e. The target carries the specifically transported right coaction. This preserves the stability condition of [Milne’s definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); the local coaction choice is essential, rather than an arbitrary structure already on that module. Checks pass: [transportOrderIso_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Transport.lean#L115), [transportInvHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L207).
Checks the inverse subcomodule image.
Checks the inverse morphism has underlying map e⁻¹.

A linear equivalence e:M≃N identifies their subcomodule orders after N is given the transported coaction (e⊗id_C)ρe⁻¹. Images under e and e⁻¹ are inverse and preserve containment. This carries [Milne’s stability condition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) to the new module; it does not assert the same for an unrelated pre-existing coaction on N. Checks pass: [transportOrderIso_apply_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Transport.lean#L123), [transportOrderIso_symm_apply_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Transport.lean#L132).
Checks the forward carrier map.
Checks the inverse carrier map.

The forward subcomodule correspondence under transport is image under e, viewed as a comodule morphism to the module with coaction (e⊗id_C)ρe⁻¹. This is the direct-image interpretation of [Milne’s stability condition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The explicitly installed target coaction makes e colinear; a bare linear equivalence between arbitrary fixed coactions would not suffice. Checks pass: [transportOrderIso_apply_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Transport.lean#L123), [transportToHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L215).
Checks the corresponding ordinary module image.
Checks the forward morphism evaluates as e.

The inverse correspondence sends a subcomodule of the transported module to its image under e⁻¹. The inverse map is colinear because the target’s coaction was defined by conjugating through e. This is the inverse-image interpretation of [Milne’s subcomodule notion](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), with no flatness needed because e already has a linear inverse. Checks pass: [transportOrderIso_symm_apply_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Transport.lean#L132), [transportInvHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L222).
Checks the underlying inverse image formula.
Checks the inverse morphism evaluates as e⁻¹.

Mutually inverse comodule morphisms f and g identify the ordered sets of subcomodules by taking images. Image composition and the two inverse identities prove bijectivity, while image monotonicity proves order compatibility. This preserves [Milne’s subcomodule condition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); both maps intertwine coactions, and the result requires no flatness or finite-dimensionality. Checks pass: [mapOrderIso_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Transport.lean#L72), [mapOrderIso_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Transport.lean#L82).
Checks the forward correspondence is image under f.
Checks the inverse correspondence is image under g.

Forgetting the forward transport of a subcomodule gives its ordinary module image under e. This agrees with the standard order isomorphism on submodules and preserves the coaction-stability condition in [Milne’s definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The target is equipped with the transported coaction; no equality with an unrelated coaction is assumed. Checks pass: [transportOrderIso_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Transport.lean#L108), [transportToHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L199).
Checks transport uses the forward comodule morphism.
Checks that morphism’s underlying map is e.

Real exponentiation notation uses Lean’s real power function, with both base and exponent real. Positive bases have the usual exponential formula. The operation is also defined at zero and negative bases; those assigned values do not make every familiar exponent law unconditional. This instance installs the notation, while separate theorems state the hypotheses needed for each law. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L37).

For positive x, real exponentiation is exp(y·log x). Lean extends it by setting 0^0=1 and 0^y=0 for nonzero y. For negative x it takes the real part of the principal complex power, namely exp(y·log|x|)·cos(πy). This is a specified extension, not the convention that negative bases admit ordinary real odd roots. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L34).

A strictly positive real base raised to any real exponent remains strictly positive. This includes negative and zero exponents, since the result is an exponential. The hypothesis excludes zero, whose nonzero powers are assigned zero, and negative bases, whose real-power extension can vanish or be negative. No restriction on the exponent is required. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L116).

Every real power of a nonnegative real base is nonnegative, with no sign restriction on the exponent. At a positive base this follows from the exponential formula. At zero the assigned result is either 1 or 0, including for negative exponents. The statement does not assert this for negative bases, whose powers may be negative. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L163).

When a natural-number exponent is viewed as a real number, Lean’s real power agrees with repeated multiplication. The base can be any real number, including a negative number or zero. Exponent zero gives the empty product 1 in both operations. The cast changes the exponent’s type, not its value; it performs no rounding. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L61).

For an integer exponent, viewed as a real number, real exponentiation agrees with integer powers of any real base. Negative integer powers use reciprocals. This also holds at zero because Lean defines the reciprocal of zero as zero: zero to a negative integer is therefore zero in both operations, while exponent zero gives 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L56).

Raising any real number to real exponent 1 returns that number. No positivity hypothesis is needed: at a negative base the cosine factor contributes the negative sign, and at zero the assigned power is zero. Thus real exponentiation agrees with the ordinary first power across its entire domain, despite its special treatment of other noninteger exponents. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L148).

Every real number raised to real exponent zero equals 1, including zero and negative bases. In particular, 0^0 is deliberately assigned the empty-product value 1. This is a value of Lean’s everywhere-defined power operation; it is not a claim that a limit involving independently varying base and exponent must equal 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L120).

The positive real base 1 raised to any real exponent is 1. The exponent can be irrational, negative, or zero; the positive-base formula reduces to exp(y·log 1)=exp 0. This concerns a fixed base of exactly 1, so it says nothing about limits in which a varying base approaches 1 while the exponent grows. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L154).

Zero raised to any nonzero real exponent is defined as zero. Negative exponents are included: in this finite real-number type, 0^(−1)=0 rather than infinity or an undefined value. The nonzero-exponent hypothesis is essential because 0^0=1. This theorem records Lean’s explicit extension outside the usual domain of negative powers. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L128).

For a strictly positive real base, adding two arbitrary real exponents multiplies the corresponding powers: x^(y+z)=x^y·x^z. The base condition matters under Lean’s conventions. At zero with exponents 1 and −1, the left side is 1 while the right side is zero. Negative bases likewise require additional restrictions for such laws. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L207).

The exponent-addition law also holds for a nonnegative base when the sum of the exponents is nonzero. This permits a zero base: then at least one factor vanishes, and the power on the left vanishes too. Excluding a zero sum prevents failures such as 0^(1−1)=1 but 0^1·0^(−1)=0. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L210).

For a nonnegative real base, increasing the exponent by 1 multiplies the power by the base, provided the new exponent is nonzero. Zero bases are allowed. The excluded exponent is y=−1: at zero, the proposed equality would read 1=0. For positive bases this restriction is unnecessary, but this version explicitly covers zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L458).

For a nonnegative real base, negating the exponent takes the reciprocal of the power. Zero is allowed because Lean’s real inverse sends zero to zero: nonzero exponents give zero on both sides at that base, and exponent zero gives 1. The base restriction avoids the different behavior of real powers at negative bases. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L259).

For a nonnegative real base, multiplying two real exponents agrees with applying the corresponding powers successively. Both exponents may be negative or zero. The identity also holds at a zero base under Lean’s 0^0=1 and other zero-power defaults. Negative bases are excluded because taking real parts of complex powers does not preserve this composition law. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L414).

For a nonnegative real base and a natural number n, multiplying a real exponent y by n has the same effect as raising x^y to the ordinary nth power. The exponent y may be negative. The natural number is included exactly into the reals, with no rounding; n=0 gives 1 on both sides. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L520).

A product of two nonnegative real numbers raised to any real exponent equals the product of their powers. Zero factors and negative exponents are permitted because zero powers use Lean’s finite defaults. At exponent zero both sides equal 1. The nonnegative-base hypotheses prevent failures caused by the cosine factor assigned to negative bases. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L476).

For a nonnegative real base, taking its reciprocal and then a real power agrees with taking the power first and then its reciprocal. No nonzero condition is imposed: at zero, Lean’s reciprocal and nonzero powers are all zero, while exponent zero gives 1. This is an identity for ordinary real values, without infinity. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L485).

For nonnegative real numerator and denominator, a real power of their quotient equals the quotient of their powers. The denominator may be zero because real division by zero is defined as zero. Even then the identity holds: a nonzero exponent gives zero on both sides, while exponent zero gives 1 on both sides. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L488).

For a strictly positive real base, the logarithm of a real power is the exponent times the logarithm of the base. Every real exponent is allowed, including zero and negative values. Positivity ensures that the power is positive too, so both logarithms have their usual analytic meaning; Lean’s assigned logarithm values outside that domain are not needed. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L494).

Over a complete nonarchimedean field, an overconvergent series distinguished in Y of degree s, with invertible degree-s coefficient, uniquely factors as eω. Both e and its inverse are overconvergent; ω is monic of degree s with overconvergent coefficients in the other variables. Its Gauss norm is automatically one. When s=0, ω=1. See [Grosse-Klönne §1.3(ii), p.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1408.3329#page=3). Checks pass through [unequal-radius selection](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/Distinguished.lean#L199), [explicit monic-factor uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/Preparation.lean#L56) for Y+X² and Y+p, and [the unit criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/WashnitzerAlgebra.lean#L528) for 1+pY and Y−p⁻¹. These are specializations of existing formulas.
Existing uniqueness identifies the explicit unit and monic factors
The monic factor has exactly unit Gauss norm
Complete coefficient rings at unequal radii support preparation
An overconvergent unit retains an overconvergent inverse
The factorization also holds in the overconvergent algebra itself

Over a complete ultrametric commutative ring with multiplicative norm, a restricted series distinguished of degree s at radius c>0, with invertible degree-s coefficient, uniquely factors as eω. Here e and its inverse converge at that radius, while ω is monic of degree s. Earlier weighted coefficients may tie for the maximum; s=0 forces ω=1. See [Martin, Corollary1.28, pp.2422–2423](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32152#page=18). Checks pass: [the computed X−b family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/GaussNorm.lean#L561) at c=1 and c=√p, [factor uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Weierstrass/Preparation.lean#L425), and [zero remainder in degree zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Weierstrass/DivMod.lean#L257). These are mathematical specializations; the nonzero dual-number check lies outside the multiplicative-norm hypotheses.
The computed linear family includes X−1 at radii1 and√p
Existing uniqueness identifies a monic polynomial’s preparation
Degree-zero division has zero remainder
The monic factor inherits distinguishedness and its normalized Gauss norm
